description: The barometric formula gives air pressure at any altitude (below 11,000 m) from sea-level pressure — in hPa, inHg and percent of sea level.

faqs.a: P = P₀ × (1 − 0.0065·h/288.15)^5.25588, with h in metres — the standard-atmosphere barometric formula, valid below 11,000 m (the tropopause).
Sea-level pressure varies with weather around 1013.25 hPa (the ISA standard). Enter your local sea-level (QNH) pressure for the most accurate result.
faqs.q: What sea-level pressure should I enter?

faqs.a: The formula assumes the standard troposphere lapse rate of 6.5 °C per km and stops being valid above the tropopause (11,000 m).
faqs.q: Why is there an 11,000 m limit?

howto: Enter the altitude in metres or feet.
Read the pressure at altitude in hPa, inHg and as a percent of sea level.
